external_invariants: The full fixed-length generation must complete: one prefill forward plus exactly new_tokens-1 cached decode steps; EOS early stopping is disabled by the explicit loop and the decode loop must not be truncated or batched differently (qwen_inference.py:25-32).
Greedy decoding only: every step takes argmax over the last-position logits of the previous step's token; no sampling or beam search.
use_cache=True with the KV cache carried across decode steps, and logits_to_keep=1 so only the last position's logits are materialized (prefill and every decode step).

Numerical policy is fixed: BF16 weights with attn_implementation='sdpa', TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark False, torch.manual_seed(20261020), set_num_threads(4), set_num_interop_threads(1) (qwen_inference.py:49, common.py:34-42).

Inputs are the chat-templated fixed prompt tokens repeated/truncated to exactly 256 tokens, batch=1, resident on the bound GPU before timing; tokenization and host-to-device transfer are setup, not timed.

The first-token boundary is the source's explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() after prefill forward + argmax (qwen_inference.py:16-24); ttft_ms, decode_ms, end_to_end_ms, decode_tokens_per_second (batch*(new_tokens-1)/decode interval) and generated_tokens_per_second (batch*new_tokens/end-to-end interval) all come from perf_counter_ns around these source boundaries and must keep those exact semantics.

Correctness checks: generated greedy tokens must satisfy torch.equal exactly (no tolerance), and the captured per-step last-token logits stacked to [batch, new_tokens, vocab] are compared with torch.testing.assert_close at atol=rtol=0.02 (common.py:74-76, qwen_inference.py:61-62); the +1 corruption negative control must be rejected (common.py:79-84).

Model loading, tokenization, input construction, reference capture runs (including the teacher-forced second pass), correctness checks, {id}-reference.pt saving, warmup, repeats, summarize() and --profile tracing are benchmark-harness setup or measurement infrastructure outside the timed unit and are not repeated inside run().

Single-process single-GPU task: the model is placed on the worker-provided device, there is no process group and no NCCL communication, and the adapter must not initialize another process group or allocate a second reference model on GPU.

All mutable per-run state (KV cache, generated-token list, per-step logits list) is created inside run and released with it; nothing is pre-cleared or pre-warmed across the measured boundary that the source itself does inside infer().

selection.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms: the source-measured wall interval from the pre-forward synchronize to the first-token-ready synchronize after prefill+argmax (qwen_inference.py:16-24), so only prefill-phase execution is in the timed window; decode (727.9 ms of the 753.2 ms unit) is outside it and is a separate goal, not a constraint. Measured facts: clean baseline ttft_ms=25.799 (project.json original_baseline rank 0); the prefill-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM subtree accounts for 21.62 ms of nested diagnostic CUDA time (torch trace, e0861b46dbeeb562f67f), leaving ~4.2 ms (~16%) of the clean wall as eager host-dispatch/launch gap for 2145 single-stream kernel launches in the first-token window (nsys: GPU busy 21.46 ms, busy fraction 0.51 in the perturbed 41.8 ms window, 20.3 ms total inter-kernel gaps, largest 0.57/0.51/0.50/0.48 ms; python_runtime shows the host cost in the nn.Module call chain - 17,472 module calls - and 9,376 TensorBase.to dispatches). Within the 21.5 ms busy time, GEMMs are ~15.2 ms on RTX 4090 (AD102) at ~150 TFLOP/s effective bf16 - near roofline, low-yield to replace - and SDPA flash is only 0.74 ms; the remaining ~4.4 ms is many small elementwise/reduce/copy kernels per layer: RMSNorm float32 chains (mean/pow/rsqrt, 145 launches each, 560/308/151 us), rotary bf16<->fp32 conversions (aten::to.dtype, 293 calls, 676 us), KV-cache CatArrayBatchedCopy (144 launches, 531 us), direct copies (452 us), mul (471 calls, 1.37 ms) and add (254 calls, 0.51 ms). The selected region is the coherent editable boundary covering exactly the prefill-phase model forward subtree (52 module groups: Qwen3ForCausalLM/Qwen3Model/Qwen3DecoderLayer/Qwen3Attention x36/Qwen3MLP/Linear x6/Qwen3RMSNorm x3/SiLU/Rotary/Embedding, plus 73 aten functional groups inside that span, 2982 calls); discovery-only profiler:: groups and all decode/run-phase groups are excluded so the replacement can be phase-guarded to prefill while the 31 cached decode steps, their groups, the workload length, measurement boundaries and single-GPU no-communication setup stay untouched.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing this prefill region with a leaner equivalent implementation - fusing the per-layer RMSNorm float32 chain and residual add, applying rotary from precomputed/reused cos/sin without per-layer dtype round-trips, writing K/V directly into preallocated cache positions instead of cat, and flattening the Python dispatch path - will remove a large fraction of the ~4.4 ms small-kernel GPU time and part of the ~4.2 ms launch-gap share by cutting both kernel count and host dispatches per layer, while GEMMs and SDPA keep their current cuBLAS/flash kernels. Expected effect (hypothesis to test, not a promise): ttft_ms drops ~15-25% from 25.8 ms toward ~19.5-22 ms, with exact greedy tokens and per-step logits within atol=rtol=0.02 preserved by keeping float32 accumulation semantics in the fused norm/rotary math and by returning a KV cache object the unmodified decode steps can consume unchanged. Risks: the clean-run gap share may be smaller than the perturbed nsys/cProfile views suggest; any fusion-induced rounding change could flip an argmax tie (torch.equal is exact); the replacement must be guarded to the prefill phase only, and decode-phase groups and the argmax/cat calls outside the model forward are deliberately not selected because the proposal does not affect them.

proposal.rationale: Objective ttft_ms is the source wall interval from the pre-forward synchronize to the first-token-ready synchronize after prefill+argmax, so only the prefill-phase model forward is timed; the 31 cached decode steps are outside it and are a separate goal. Measured facts: clean baseline ttft_ms=25.799 (project.json original_baseline rank 0); the prefill-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM subtree (target-resources.json c9d14173dd4887d4a4133553) accounts for 21.62 ms of CUDA time over 2145 single-stream kernel launches, all prefill; the nsys first-token window (observations/current/nsys-9ed9145c.json) shows 41.75 ms perturbed wall, 21.46 ms GPU busy (51.4%), 20.3 ms of inter-kernel gaps with 1117 gaps >5 us and largest gaps 0.57/0.51/0.50/0.48 ms on one stream, i.e. the clean ~25.8 ms window carries an eager host-dispatch/launch-gap share of roughly 4 ms; python_runtime (observations/current/python_runtime-aea48e29.json) shows the eager host chain: 17,472 nn.Module _wrapped_call_impl calls, 9,376 TensorBase.to dispatches and 8,096 linear calls. GEMMs are ~15.3 ms (71%) of the window's kernel time on RTX 4090 at bf16, near roofline, so re-authoring math has low yield and high numeric risk against the exact-greedy-token requirement. Route chosen: replace only the region root - the prefill-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM module boundary - with a CUDA-Graph replay of the accepted parent forward. On the first eligible invocation (inside the adapter's real prefill phase, so inherited dispatch and phase semantics are exactly what gets captured) the replacement warms the parent 3x on a side stream, captures context.references[call_id] into a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph, replays once and validates bitwise equality of the logits and all 36 layers' K/V against the eager parent output on the same static input. Every later invocation copies the current input_ids into the 2 KB static buffer and replays: the identical 2145 kernels re-execute on the current input contents, so the workload executes on each invocation and nothing is precomputed - this removes the eager Python dispatch chain and per-launch gaps while keeping kernel-level numerics bitwise equal to the parent (validated at capture time), which protects torch.equal greedy tokens and the 0.02 logits tolerance. The returned object clones the static logits and per-layer K/V into fresh tensors and wraps them in a new DynamicCache, so the unmodified decode steps consume parent-identical cache values with no cross-invocation aliasing; decode phase is untouched (its boundary is not replaced and its signature past_key_values!=None also fails the guard). Expected effect (hypothesis to be measured, not a promise): ttft_ms approaches the ~21.6 ms GPU busy time plus ~0.1 ms of copy/clone overhead, roughly a 13-16% reduction, with decode_tokens_per_second unchanged. Fallbacks are individually labeled via context['record_route']: cuda_graph_replay / cuda_graph_capture on the graph path, parent_fallback_signature for non-matching calls (any 2D CUDA int input with use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1, empty cache and no extra kwargs can build its own keyed graph; other shapes/signatures fall back), parent_fallback_context for grad-enabled or foreign-capture contexts, parent_fallback_setup_failure and parent_fallback_runtime_failure keep concise failure categories and permanently restore the parent route. No inputs/previous-feedback.txt or inputs/previous-candidate exists, so this attempt has no prior feedback to incorporate; installed_bundles in search.json is empty, so requires/replaces are empty and no earlier bundle is superseded.
proposal.setup_work: All setup is lazy inside the first eligible prefill invocation (warmup=2 precedes the timed repeats, and the quality/coverage execution happens first, so capture cost does not land in clean repeats). Setup steps: (1) allocate a static input buffer (2 KB int64) and run the parent forward 3x eagerly on a side stream; (2) capture the parent forward with torch.cuda.graph into a CUDAGraph - allocations during capture come from the graph's private pool; (3) replay once, synchronize, and bitwise-compare logits plus all 36 K/V tensor pairs against the eager warmup output (any mismatch raises, falls back to the parent and is reported as a setup failure). Retained for the process lifetime: the CUDAGraph with its private pool (peak concurrent prefill intermediates of the 256-token forward plus the 36x512KB K and 36x512KB V static tensors ~36 MB and one ~0.3 MB static logits tensor) and the 2 KB static input. Per steady-state invocation the replacement adds: 2 KB device-to-device input copy, one graph launch, a logits clone (~0.3 MB) and a 36 MB K/V clone via torch._foreach_copy_ into freshly allocated tensors (allocator refcounting preserves alias semantics; candidate-owned static buffers are the only memory overwritten between invocations). Memory-scope note: warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes should be comparable or slightly lower than baseline (eager prefill transients disappear, +36.3 MB permanently-live static tensors), while reserved and lifecycle peaks increase by the retained graph pool; no counter change is claimed as a general physical-memory saving. Setup performs no fixture-dependent precomputation and caches no outputs.
quality_risks: Numerics: graph replay re-executes the same captured kernels with the same arguments, so outputs are bitwise identical to the eager parent; this is validated at capture time against the eager warmup run (logits and all K/V pairs, torch.equal) and any mismatch disables the graph path. Exact greedy tokens (torch.equal) and the 0.02 logits tolerance therefore face no new rounding risk on the graph path.

Coverage: CUDA Graph replay does not re-run Python hooks, so the 3641 inner prefill call sites of the selected region no longer appear as observed Python invocations (listed in eliminated_calls); their work still executes natively inside the replayed graph on every invocation (graph node ids visible in any later kernel trace), and the replaced region root boundary itself is invoked once per prefill and self-reports its route via record_route. Consumers of the eliminated inner calls are only the captured graph itself, whose outputs feed the cloned logits and DynamicCache returned to the adapter.

Capture risk: if any op in the parent forward were capture-unsafe, torch.cuda.graph raises during setup; the replacement then permanently routes to the parent (parent_fallback_setup_failure) and behavior equals the baseline. The same applies to runtime failures (parent_fallback_runtime_failure).

First-invocation cost: warmup+capture+validation (~4 extra forwards) is paid once in the quality/warmup invocation, not in the timed repeats (warmup=2); lazy setup inside a real invocation is used so the captured work is the accepted parent's work under active phases, per the binding contract.

State/alias: each invocation receives freshly cloned logits and K/V tensors in a newly constructed DynamicCache (config-driven, same layer class), so decode cat() semantics, reset behavior and continuous multi-invocation execution match the parent; only candidate-owned static pool buffers are reused across invocations. Decode-phase and non-matching signatures always run the parent.
The decode goal is untouched: prefill replay returns bitwise parent-identical K/V, so the 31 decode steps produce the same logits/tokens as baseline; no sampling, batching or length semantics change.

plan.rationale: Frozen objective is ttft_ms on a single-GPU, single-process Qwen3-4B inference (batch=1, 256 prompt tokens, eager sdpa, explicit synchronize at the first-token-ready boundary). The torch collector already ran: coverage.json shows 66441/66441 CUDA kernels associated with 0 unassociated and 0 ambiguous forward sequences, so kernel attribution and overlap questions are already resolved and nsys would add nothing; there are no CUDA graphs or NCCL waits to separate (communication capability is not_applicable 'single-device task'), so nsys, nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and device_telemetry (device-wide native-window samples that cannot resolve a ~25 ms prefill window) are not selected. The observed uncertainty in evaluation.json/revisions.json is twofold. First, the only listed candidate (revision a00f1d61..., parent b759f428...) measured objective 24.755876 ms vs paired parent 24.886221 ms and was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise, while its binding summary shows requested legacy but effective direct with reason 'no functional replacements' - an additive candidate that did not replace the parent, so binding_cost is applicable and its clean AB/BA parent vs binding-only passthrough comparison with full quality checks will establish whether the binding layer contributes any of the noise-level delta or whether the ~0.13 ms difference is run-to-run noise of the parent path. Second, with ~25 ms TTFT under eager dispatch of tens of thousands of small kernels per run, whether the prefill window is host-submit-bound or GPU-bound decides which further reductions can matter: execution_timeline records a separate plain Torch trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization at the explicit first-token boundary, and per-device intervals to measure idle gaps vs kernel occupancy inside the TTFT window (with clock alignment bounds for matched submissions only), and python_runtime's warmed cProfile then attributes host dispatch and binding call costs by function, read qualitatively since it perturbs execution. The plan pins revision to the exact candidate ID a00f1d61fb09e2ecb3a13f065428cc022d0b40b5c82f7058374294929c9d955f; all selected collectors run on this exact candidate in separate workers and none of them replaces a communication hook or drives any prescribed optimization action.
